reasoning_traces.think:
The core of causal inference lies in translating observational queries into interventional ones through adjustment sets, front-door, and back-door criteria. Do-calculus provides a formalism for computing interventional expectations from observational data, requiring conditional mean tables and adjustment sets. Back-door set discovery identifies valid conditioning sets to block confounding paths. Temporal causal discovery extracts lagged dependencies from time series to infer causal directionality. These primitives form a kernel of causal reasoning where each step must satisfy graphical criteria and statistical identifiability. Failure occurs when adjustment sets are not identified, or when temporal structures violate stationarity assumptions. The absence of residual mining indicates a gap in post-hoc model diagnostics rather than fundamental algorithmic incompleteness.
